newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives' EU split could hit jobs-Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives' EU split could hit jobs-Labour.

text.p: The main opposition Labour party warned on Thursday that growing anti-European sentiment in the ruling Conservative party could scare foreign investors away from Britain.

Labour leader Tony Blair and industry spokeswoman Margaret Beckett seized on a report in The Times newspaper that Japanese car giant Toyota was worried that some Conservative "Euro-sceptics" wanted to pull out of the European Union.
"It would be of great concern to Toyota if the UK found itself excluded from the European Union," Alan Marsh, vice-chairman of Toyota Motor Europe, told the paper.

Leaving the EU would have "serious consequences for Toyota in the UK", he added. Toyota last year built 117,000 cars at its plant in Derbyshire, central England, and is considering how rapidly to expand production there.

Blair, in a pep-talk to Labour candidates at the coming election, said the Conservatives were so deeply divided under Prime Minister John Major that they were no longer capable of representing Britain's interests either at home or in Europe.

Referring to the Toyota report, he added: "People know that Britain has to be part of Europe, standing up for British interests but understanding that being a key leading player in Europe is in Britain's interests... for jobs, for investment and for our infleunce and standing in the world."

Beckett said the danger of Conservative Euro-sceptics advancing the cause of EU withdrawal was the biggest threat to British jobs and investment -- and not, as Major claimed, the EU's Social Chapter legislation on workplace standards.

"It is a serious worry for many in British business that the prime minister's dithering, inconsistent and cowardly handling of his own party's catastrophic division on this matter is itself doing great harm to Britain," Beckett said.
